entities.summary: Jean IV de Beaumont (1318-07-01) was a Marshal of France who played a pivotal role in the Hundred Years' War. He led the French forces to a decisive victory at the Battle of Poitiers in 1356, where the English were defeated and the French were taken prisoner. This event marked a turning point in the war, leading to the French resurgence and the eventual defeat of the English at the Battle of Castillon in 1453. As a result, Beaumont's name became synonymous with French military prowess and his legacy continued to shape French history for centuries to come. The Battle of Poitiers also had significant economic and political consequences, as the English were forced to pay a large ransom to secure the release of the French prisoners, further straining the English economy. Furthermore, the victory at Poitiers marked a significant shift in the balance of power between France and England, paving the way for future French victories and cementing Beaumont's place as one of the most important figures of the Hundred Years' War. Beaumont's military achievements were also marked by his innovative tactics and his ability to adapt to changing circumstances on the battlefield. He was a key figure in the development of the French military tradition, which would go on to influence military strategy and tactics for centuries to come. The legacy of Beaumont can also be seen in the many French military leaders who followed in his footsteps, including the famous Joan of Arc, who was inspired by Beaumont's military victories and went on to lead the French army to several victories during the Hundred Years' War. Through his military campaigns and his innovative tactics, Beaumont played a significant role in shaping the course of French history and leaving a lasting legacy that continues to be felt today.
